entries.note: O'Hare 2009 Cancer Cell (PMID 19878872) resolves; quote verbatim in abstract. Opening untested entry at 2009 is correct.
Cortes 2012 NEJM (PMC3777383) full text has the pCRKL sentence verbatim. Model-side CRKL readout seen only at abstract level (O'Hare full text rate-limited); proximal tier fine.
Quote verbatim but abstract does not state 40 nM; the 40 nM screen threshold is confirmed by Cortes 2012 full text ('ponatinib suppressed the emergence of any mutation at a concentration of 40 nM').
Quote verbatim in Cortes 2012 full text; source itself sets trough against the 40 nM screen threshold, so comparison_stated true is right. margin_stated null correct (FDA PharmR states no margin).
PACE abstract (PMID 24180494) verbatim; MCyR in CP-CML is the primary endpoint. NCT01207440 results first posted 2020-01-29, matches registry_date; year 2013 from epub is right.

Zhang CCR 2020 (epub 2020-09-14) verbatim; MMR6 is primary. Luo 2010 Leukemia (HH-GV-678) resolves, no abstract, prediction known only from title. Sharing model_id with ponatinib's model is a call; see rule questions.
Abstract verbatim; patient-level opening entry fine.

PACE abstract verbatim; also 'Responses were observed regardless of the baseline BCR-ABL kinase domain mutation status'. Same holds for 2013, but Zabriskie 2014 compound-mutation resistance is a missing later entry on this track (see missing).

entries.rule: safety: 'did the model's stated prediction hold, or was its silence contradicted on a harm the species could have shown'; one contra beats a same on the track
entries.note: Quote verbatim in bundled PharmR. PharmR has zero hits for thromb/occlus; 2012 label boxes ARTERIAL THROMBOSIS (8%). Rat/monkey could show vascular occlusion, so silence on the boxed harm is a miss, not partial.
entries.adjudication_note: Safety rule: silence on a harm the species could have shown is a miss. Arterial thrombosis, boxed on the 2012 label, is absent from the rat/monkey PharmR and observable in those species; a missed boxed harm outweighs partial organ matches.

entries.note: Zabriskie 2014 Cancer Cell (PMC4160372) highlights carry the quote verbatim; opening untested entry at the panel's first use, 2014, patient level. Confirmed.
Quote verbatim in PMC4160372 highlights. Mutants were picked from clinically reported cases with outcomes already known, so retro (retrodiction true), not same. Confirmed.
Sharma 2017 Sci Transl Med (PMC5409837) quote verbatim. Opening untested entry fine; note Talbert 2015 hiPSC-CM ponatinib screen predates it, so first use year could be 2015.
Quote verbatim in PMC5409837. Ponatinib vascular toxicity was known (2013 label/PACE) before the hiPSC-EC assay, so retro is right; class-level prediction. Confirmed.
Mian 2015 Leukemia (epub 2014-11-14) abstract carries the quote verbatim; selectivity-for-safety design stated before vamotinib's trial. Opening untested entry, 2014. Confirmed.

Turkina 2025 (PMC12141164) quote verbatim; phase 1 reported no vascular occlusive or arterial events, ABI normal. Prediction (2014) preceded trial, so same, not retro; low confidence apt (n=51, ~6 months).

Zabriskie 2014 (PMC4160372) intro carries quote (citation stripped in BioC). O'Hare 2009 full text (PMC2804470): T315I-start screen kept E255V/T315I to 320 nM, above 101 nM plasma level; 2009 screen predates 2014 failures, so prospective same, not retro.

missing: Patient-level track, later entry: Zabriskie 2014 Cancer Cell (doi:10.1016/j.ccr.2014.07.006, PMC4160372) shows T315I-inclusive compound mutants (E255V/T315I IC50 659.5 nM, >6.5x mean 45 mg plasma level) caused clinical ponatinib resistance, against the 2009 screen's 'completely abrogated resistance' at 40 nM; candidate contra (or same/partial, since the paper says preclinical studies had flagged compound-mutant vulnerability) in 2014.

Missing track: Ba/F3 compound-mutant in-vitro resistance profiling (Zabriskie 2014: 'In vitro resistance profiling was predictive of treatment outcomes in Ph(+) leukemia patients'), patient-level; largely a retrodiction since built on clinically reported mutants.

Missing track: ex vivo drug-sensitivity profiling of patient leukemia cells, 'Drug response profiling can predict response to ponatinib in a patient' (Blood Cancer J 2015, https://www.nature.com/articles/bcj201513), patient-level, single case.

Missing failure: EPIC phase 3 ponatinib vs imatinib first-line (NCT01650805; Lipton 2016 Lancet Oncol, doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(16)00080-2, PMID 27083332) terminated early for arterial occlusive events (7% vs 2%); primary endpoint not evaluable. Bears on safety (thrombosis) and should be noted in efficacy.

Missing dose evidence: OPTIC dose-ranging (Cortes 2021 Blood, PMC9728404) kept responses after reduction to 15 mg, whose trough is below the 40 nM screen threshold; relevant to whether the screen's exposure target was over-stated.
Vamotinib's own preclinical model (Mian 2015 Leukemia, PF-114 in Ba/F3 T315I and mouse) is cited by Turkina 2025; draft records vamotinib only under patient_trials without naming this model source.
rule_questions: Safety: when an animal study matches some clinical organ toxicities (heart, liver, pancreas) but is silent on the boxed harm (arterial thrombosis) the species could show, is the cell same+partial or contra?

Does a member drug's own preclinical model (flumatinib's HH-GV-678 cell/mouse work, vamotinib's PF-114 work) share the track of another member's model of the same type, or is it its own track ('a member drug's own model' is listed as a missing-track type)?

Dose: a screen-stated exposure target was reached (same), but a later trial (OPTIC) showed efficacy below it. Is that an over-prediction (source_calls_it over_predicted / magnitude) on the dose track or out of scope because the target was reached?

Patient-level mutation track: when the screen flagged compound-mutant vulnerability but its headline claim was complete suppression at 40 nM, does later clinical compound-mutant escape at above-40 nM exposure score contra or same/partial?
Can a short (median ~6 months, n=51) phase 1 with no arterial occlusive events score `same` for a vascular-safety prediction when the reference drug's events accrued over years (vamotinib safety 5)?
